title: Pre-colonial forest use
description: Forests in India and other regions are used by tribal and village communities for shifting cultivation, grazing, hunting, and collecting forest produce under customary rights.

title: Expansion of colonial rule
description: British colonial control expands in India, increasing demand for timber for ships, railways, and public works.

title: Railway expansion begins
description: Large-scale railway construction increases demand for wood, especially teak and sal, leading to large-scale forest exploitation.

title: Forest Department set up
description: The British establish the Imperial Forest Department in India to manage and control forests scientifically for commercial use.

title: First Indian Forest Act
description: The first Forest Act is passed to declare forests as government property and restrict traditional community use.

title: Revised Forest Act
description: Forests are classified into Reserved, Protected, and Village forests; most rights of local people are taken away in Reserved forests.

title: Forest Policy
description: The British government declares forests as a national resource meant to serve imperial needs rather than local communities.

title: Impact on forest dwellers
description: Shifting cultivation, grazing, and forest-based livelihoods are restricted, forcing many tribal communities into poverty and rebellion.

title: Forest rebellions
description: Tribal and peasant communities in Bastar and other regions revolt against forest laws and colonial control.

title: Indian Forest Act of 1927
description: A new law further strengthens government control over forests and continues restrictions on community use.

title: Independence of India
description: British rule ends, but many colonial forest laws and practices continue in independent India.

title: New awareness about forests
description: People’s movements begin demanding conservation, tribal rights, and protection of forests from commercial exploitation.

title: Forest Conservation Act
description: The Indian government passes a law to restrict deforestation and promote conservation of forest resources.

title: Forest Rights Act
description: Traditional rights of forest-dwelling communities are legally recognized and restored.
